moduleTitle: Lesson 1 - Mobile Engine 3.0 & the Tricentis Mobile Agent
learningObjectives: Describe what the Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA) does and what manual toolchain work it removes.
Explain how Mobile Engine 3.0 relates to Appium under the hood without exposing that complexity to the tester.
List the platforms and app types Mobile Engine 3.0 supports.
Distinguish the roles of TMA (device/session management) from Mobile Engine 3.0 (steering and TestCase execution).

elements.description: Direct Appium setup can require the server, selected platform drivers and their dependencies. Exact requirements depend on driver, host and version. TMA bundles the supported Appium layer, but device authorization, platform preparation and compatibility checks remain necessary.

elements.term: TMA removes the toolchain, not the underlying engine
elements.description: TMA simplifies Appium/Java/environment-variable setup for supported devices. Appium drivers and platform tooling still impose compatibility and preparation requirements; use the Agent-certified versions rather than replacing them with arbitrary latest drivers.

elements.text: Session logs and Desired Capabilities may expose Appium details. Normal Tosca authoring uses Modules, but troubleshooting or advanced capabilities can require understanding that underlying layer.

bulletPoints: No manual Appium, Java, or environment-variable setup — TMA owns that layer.
Underneath: UiAutomator2 for Android, XCUITest for iOS — visible mainly in error messages, not in daily use.

elements.description: TMA is a separate installation that manages mobile connectivity and exposes connected device information. Use its Device management view and relevant logs to inspect targets. A displayed device alone is not proof that a session or every subsequent action will succeed.

Mobile Engine 3.0 provides the Tosca mobile workflow; mobile web scanning/execution uses Mobile Web Engine 3.0. Modules, TestSteps and ActionModes remain familiar, while app type, capabilities, controls and session preparation affect execution.

elements.title: Division of responsibility
items: TMA: supported device connectivity and Appium setup; inspect targets and prepare the platform.
Mobile Engine 3.0: control identification during Mobile Scan, and steering (click, swipe, type, verify) during TestCase execution.
Tosca Commander: where Modules and TestCases are authored, exactly as with any other Engine.

bulletPoints: TMA = the device/session layer. Mobile Engine 3.0 = the steering layer. Tosca Commander = where you build and run TestCases.

elements.title: What Mobile Engine 3.0 automates
items: Android — physical devices (via USB) and emulators created through Android Studio.
iOS — physical devices and simulators, with host/Xcode requirements from the installed Agent version; TMA 2025.4 lists macOS hosts.
Native apps — built specifically for the platform, e.g. a compiled Android/iOS app.
Hybrid apps — a native shell hosting embedded web views, common in cross-platform frameworks.
Mobile web — a website opened in the device's own browser, scanned in its device context.

elements.text: Native, hybrid and web apps share the mobile workflow, but not every scanning engine, opening Module or supported control. Mobile Web Engine 3.0 handles web content; the native path differs.

bulletPoints: Android/iOS with version-scoped support; native, hybrid and mobile web with app-specific scanning and steering.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Local vs Remote — a first look

elements.description: Local (TMA) connects a supported local target to the Tosca/Agent host. Android emulators run with the Agent. Validate host/platform support for the installed version.

TMA runs on a different machine than Tosca Commander — for example a Mac running TMA for iOS work, connected to over the network from a Windows machine running Tosca Commander. Remote is also how shared device farms and CI environments are typically wired.

elements.text: This is only an introduction — the full connection mechanics (TCPs, the TMAServer trailing-slash requirement, the --rest-address startup flag) are covered in depth in the Connecting Tosca to TMA lesson.

bulletPoints: Local = TMA and Tosca Commander on the same machine. Remote = TMA on a different machine, reached over the network.
The authoring model is shared; device/app compatibility, TCPs and capabilities may require changes.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Appium must be installed and configured manually
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Setting up Appium, Java components, and environment variables before starting mobile automation in Tosca.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TMA exists precisely to remove that work — it provides simplified setup and configuration of iOS and Android devices without requiring manual Appium, Java, or environment-variable configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Treating TMA and Mobile Engine 3.0 as the same thing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Referring to 'TMA' when describing how a TestCase steers a control, or to 'Mobile Engine' when describing device connectivity.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate connectivity/session setup from scanning/steering while diagnosing. A recognition symptom can also originate in app exposure, context, permissions or the driver; the layer distinction alone does not prove which component is defective.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting iOS automation to work the same way on Windows as Android
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Trying to run TMA for iOS directly on a Windows machine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the TMA version-specific host matrix. TMA 2025.4 lists iOS hosting as macOS only; a Windows Tosca workstation can use a remote supported Mac Agent.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary job of the Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA)?

options.text: Authoring TestCases and Modules.
Simplifying mobile device connectivity and Appium/Java/environment-variable setup.
Rendering the mobile app's UI inside Tosca Commander.
Replacing the Mobile Scan entirely.

practiceQuiz.hint: TMA is the setup/connectivity layer, not the authoring layer.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA simplifies supported device connectivity and the bundled Appium setup. Platform/device preparation still applies; authoring is performed in Tosca.

optionExplanations.A: Modules and TestCases are authored in Tosca; TMA supplies connectivity/setup.
optionExplanations.B: TMA simplifies the supported mobile connection/toolchain layer; platform preparation remains required.
optionExplanations.C: The Agent’s primary purpose is connectivity, not embedding all app interfaces in Commander.
optionExplanations.D: Mobile scanning is still needed to create Modules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which app types can Mobile Engine 3.0 automate through the Mobile Scan? (three correct answers)

options.text: Native apps
Hybrid apps (native shell with embedded web views)
Mobile web (device browser)
Desktop-only Windows applications

practiceQuiz.hint: Two platforms, three kinds of app — desktop apps belong to a different Engine (WinX/UIA).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Mobile Engine 3.0 covers native, hybrid, and mobile web apps through the same Mobile Scan. Desktop Windows applications are automated through the WinX/UIA Engine, not Mobile Engine 3.0.

optionExplanations.A: Native mobile apps are a documented application category.
optionExplanations.B: Hybrid apps combine native and web content and use the relevant mobile scanning/steering paths.
optionExplanations.C: Mobile websites use the device browser and Mobile Web Engine 3.0.
optionExplanations.D: Desktop-only applications are outside the mobile application categories.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Appium driver is associated with iOS automation and its XCTest/WebDriverAgent tooling?

options.text: UiAutomator2
XCUITest
Selenium WebDriver
A proprietary Tricentis-only protocol with no Appium relationship

practiceQuiz.hint: It is Xcode-based, which is why iOS automation needs a Mac.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Appium’s XCUITest driver uses WebDriverAgent and Apple’s XCTest tooling. Host/driver/Xcode compatibility is version-dependent; the TMA support matrix determines its supported deployment.

optionExplanations.A: UiAutomator2 is associated with Android rather than the stated iOS/XCTest tooling.
optionExplanations.B: XCUITest uses Apple XCTest through WebDriverAgent; consult compatible driver/host versions.
optionExplanations.C: Selenium WebDriver alone is not the stated iOS platform driver.
optionExplanations.D: TMA builds on Appium; it does not eliminate that relationship.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A mobile session is confirmed established, but a control is not identified correctly. Which workflow should you investigate next?

options.text: TMA, since it owns device connectivity.
Mobile Engine 3.0, since it performs control identification and steering.
Tosca Commander's licensing module.
The device's mobile network carrier.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate 'can Tosca see the device' problems from 'can Tosca recognise this control' problems.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Inspect the Mobile Scan/engine identification path, app exposure, context and underlying driver evidence. The symptom does not prove an engine defect or rule out other configuration issues.

optionExplanations.A: Established connectivity does not make TMA the sole next identification workflow to inspect.
optionExplanations.B: Inspect this identification workflow, app context and driver evidence without assuming a proven defect.
optionExplanations.C: The stated symptom does not establish a licensing failure.
optionExplanations.D: A carrier is not the identified control-scanning mechanism in the established session.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What benefit does the Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA) provide for mobile app testing?

options.text: Enhanced manual testing capabilities
Simplified supported-device connectivity and bundled Appium toolchain setup.
Support for testing only hybrid apps
Replacement of every cloud provider’s access and session configuration.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what TMA removes from the traditional mobile automation toolchain.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA simplifies its supported connectivity/toolchain setup; it does not guarantee immediate support for every latest device or replace all cloud-provider setup.

optionExplanations.A: This question concerns automation setup, not enhanced manual testing.
optionExplanations.B: Supported device/toolchain setup is simplified, but preparation and compatibility still apply.
optionExplanations.C: Native, hybrid and web are supported categories, not hybrid only.
optionExplanations.D: TMA does not universally replace cloud-provider authentication and configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following statements about Tricentis Tosca Mobile is false?

options.text: Supports documented cloud connection options with provider-specific configuration.
Simplifies supported Agent setup, while platform and device preparation remain required.
Requires every Tosca author to manually install and configure the Appium server before using TMA.
Supports testing across compatible mobile platforms, browsers and devices.

practiceQuiz.hint: One option directly contradicts what TMA exists to remove.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA bundles the supported Appium setup, so manual server setup is not a universal prerequisite. Simplification does not eliminate platform, device or provider configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Cloud options are documented; they still need provider-specific setup.
optionExplanations.B: This accurately qualifies setup simplification instead of promising no configuration.
optionExplanations.C: This false universal prerequisite contradicts TMA’s bundled setup.
optionExplanations.D: Compatible platform/browser/device testing is documented, without universal support claims.

quickRecap.value: Supported connectivity and bundled Appium setup; device preparation and compatible platform versions still matter.
Control identification (scanning) and steering (execution) inside Tosca, using the familiar Module/TestCase workflow.
UiAutomator2 (Android), XCUITest (iOS) — both Appium-standard, both hidden behind TMA in normal use.
Android/iOS targets per the installed Agent matrix; TMA 2025.4 iOS hosts are macOS.
Native, hybrid, and mobile web — one Mobile Scan handles all three.
Local = TMA + Tosca on the same machine. Remote = TMA on a different machine, reached over the network. Full mechanics in the Connecting Tosca to TMA lesson.
